translation: Shall we get started then?
We will now explain a discovered attack.

A discovered attack is a technique where one
piece is moved…

…in order to reveal an attack by a piece
previously hidden.
If this is done to aim for the king…
…it is called a discovered check.

It is hard to explain through words, so let's
take a look on the bottom screen.

Can you see how the white rook is in a
position to put the king in check…

…through the bishop?
If we now move the bishop…
…they are automatically put into check.

The black knight was always protected by
the pawn…

…but since the king is in check, it cannot
capture the bishop in return.

While the king is getting out of check, the
bishop can take…
…another pawn.

You can also use a discovered check to put
the king in check with two pieces…

…at the same time. This can lead to a
technique called a "double check.”
Here is a slightly different situation.
By putting the king in check with the bishop…

…both the bishop and the rook are putting
the king in check simultaneously.
This is called a double check.

In a double check, the opponent's king has no
choice…
…but to flee.

This is because you cannot capture two
pieces at the same time.

Let's have a go at a discovered attack
puzzle.

Capture the queen in three moves.
(Make sure you gain advantage.)
That's correct, Kyon.

That's a shame, it looks like you messed up.
Try having another go.

It looks like you didn't manage to gain
advantage.

Make sure to consider the value of each
piece, okay?
